definition: Evergage was a cloud-based software that allowed users to collect, analyze, and respond to user behavior on their websites and web applications in real-time.
details: In 2020, Evergage was acquired by Salesforce and was rebranded as Interaction Studio. The company positions itself as a "real-time personalization and customer data platform (CDP)". The company was founded as Apptegic in 2010 by Karl Wirth and Greg Hinkle, who met while working at Red Hat. In May 2012, Evergage was a finalist in the TechCrunch Disrupt Startup Battlefield and, shortly thereafter, launched its cloud-based service. In August 2013, the company changed its name to Evergage. In 2015, Evergage expanded its capabilities to include A/B and multivariate testing, as well as automated product and content recommendations driven by machine learning. The platform also added personalization support for mobile apps and, in 2016, open-time email personalization, and triggered email in 2017. Evergage acquired the e-commerce and email personalization provider MyBuys in 2018.

explainer.lead: Evergage was a cloud-based personalization and customer data platform that helped businesses react to what people were doing on their websites and apps as it happened. It combined behavior analysis with testing, recommendations, and email personalization; Salesforce acquired it in 2020 and rebranded it Interaction Studio.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a shop assistant who notices which things you look at and then shows you items that might suit you better. Evergage did something similar for websites and apps, using people’s activity to adjust recommendations and messages quickly. It could also compare different versions of content to see which worked better.
tiers.practitioner: Evergage was applied to website and web-app behavior for real-time analysis and personalization, with A/B and multivariate testing added in 2015. Teams could use its machine-learning-driven product and content recommendations, then extend personalization to mobile apps, open-time email, and triggered email. Keep testing and personalization distinct: an experiment compares variants, while a recommendation selects products or content for a user.
tiers.paperLevel: A plain-text abstraction is P(t) = f(B(t)), where B(t) represents observed user behavior and P(t) is the personalization response produced at time t. Evergage implemented this general flow in a cloud platform, using machine learning for automated product and content recommendations. A/B and multivariate testing supported comparisons of variants, while later features covered mobile apps, open-time email personalization, and triggered email.

explainer.example: A visitor browses several products on an e-commerce site. Evergage analyzes that activity and updates the page with machine-learning-driven product recommendations; the business can also run an A/B test to compare two versions of the recommendation area. If the visitor later qualifies for a follow-up, a triggered email can continue the interaction.

explainer.intuition: Instead of showing everyone the same experience, Evergage used recent behavior to decide what content, products, or messages might be more relevant to each user. Its central idea was to shorten the gap between observing an action and responding to it.
howItWorks: Collect user behavior from a website or web application.
Analyze that behavior in real time.
Choose a response, such as personalized content or a product recommendation.
Use A/B or multivariate tests to compare experience variants.
Extend personalization to mobile apps and email.
explainer.whyItMatters: Evergage brought behavior collection, real-time analysis, experimentation, and personalization into one platform. That let businesses adapt digital experiences across websites, apps, and email rather than relying only on static content.
misconceptions: Evergage was not merely a data store: it also analyzed behavior and delivered personalization, testing, and recommendations.
Open-time email personalization and triggered email are different features: one adapts content when an email is opened, while the other sends email in response to activity.
Interaction Studio was the Salesforce rebrand of Evergage after the 2020 acquisition, not the company’s original name; it was founded as Apptegic.
